## Natural history notes

A large freshwater snail characterized by a rounded brown to olive shell, an operculum “trapdoor,” and a long siphon used to breathe air while remaining partly submerged. In Florida, the Florida Apple Snail is found in marshes, sloughs, ponds, lakes, canals, ditches, wet prairies, and slow vegetated wetlands, especially in shallow areas with abundant aquatic plants. It feeds on algae, detritus, and soft aquatic vegetation, lays pinkish-white egg clusters above the waterline, and is especially important as the primary prey of Limpkins and Snail Kites.
